name: Scottish Porridge
author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors

ingredients.item: ½ cup (80 g) steel-cut oats, also called Irish oats
1 tsp lemon juice or apple cider vinegar (for soaking)
1 tsp of buckwheat flour (for reducing phytates)

steps: Mix the steel-cut oats with a tsp of buckwheat flour in a bowl.
Add warm water to soak the oats and add a splash of lemon juice or apple cider vinegar. Cover and allow to soak overnight or at least 7 to 8 hours.
Place the oats, salt and water into a small pan and gently bring it to a small boil, stirring occasionally until the porridge starts to thicken.

Once the thickening has begun, lower the heat to low to avoid burning the porridge and allow it to simmer for approximately 15 to 20 minutes (or less if the oats are tender and reached your preferred consistency).
Remove from the heat and let it stand for 1 or 2 minutes before serving.
Serve and top with your choice of toppings, such as chia seeds, walnuts, tbsp of peanut butter, berries, cinnamon, or a dollop of Greek yogurt.

culture.text: Porridge is a type of semi-solid food made by soaking, poaching or boiling, in milk or water, ground, crushed or chopped starchy plants, typically grain. It is a traditional staple food of many countries.
